blogs.title: When Behçet's Hits the Brain First: Recognizing Concurrent Neuro-BD at Presentation
blogs.description: This post explores the diagnostic challenge of simultaneous systemic BD and neuro-BD diagnosis—a rare scenario that contradicts the typical pattern of neurological involvement developing years after initial BD diagnosis. The discussion covers clinical pattern recognition, the International Criteria for Behçet's Disease scoring system, and why clinicians should maintain a low threshold for considering neuro-BD even in newly diagnosed patients presenting with headache, fever, and neurological symptoms.

blogs.title: Aseptic Meningitis with a Normal MRI: Don't Let Imaging Lull You into Missing Neuro-BD
blogs.description: A deep dive into the spectrum of neuro-BD presentations, focusing on cases like this one where brain MRI shows no parenchymal lesions despite clear CNS involvement. The post discusses how acute neuro-BD can present as isolated aseptic meningitis, the significance of CSF findings (mild lymphocytic pleocytosis, elevated protein), and why a negative MRI—particularly early in the disease course—should not exclude the diagnosis. Includes a practical approach to the differential diagnosis of aseptic meningitis.

blogs.title: SIADH and CNS Inflammation: The IL-6 Connection You Need to Know
blogs.description: This post examines the pathophysiology linking CNS inflammation to SIADH, with a focus on the IL-6–mediated mechanism proposed in this case. It discusses how inflammatory cytokines may drive dysregulated ADH secretion, the diagnostic workup for SIADH (including osmolality studies and exclusion of other causes), and why clinicians should consider SIADH in any patient with neuroinflammatory disease presenting with hyponatremia. Also addresses the distinction between disease-specific mechanisms versus non-specific CNS inflammation responses.

blogs.title: Colchicine Monotherapy for Acute Neuro-BD: Challenging the Steroid Dogma
blogs.description: A critical appraisal of current treatment paradigms for neuro-BD, which typically position corticosteroids as first-line therapy. This case demonstrated complete resolution with colchicine alone, raising questions about when immunosuppression can be avoided. The post reviews colchicine's anti-inflammatory mechanisms (neutrophil inhibition, IL-1β and IL-6 suppression), discusses the evidence for and against its use in neuro-BD, and offers practical guidance on patient selection for colchicine monotherapy versus aggressive immunosuppression.

blogs.title: Hiccups and Rhabdomyolysis: The Underappreciated Clinical Clues to Severe Hyponatremia
blogs.description: This post highlights two often-overlooked clinical manifestations of profound hyponatremia demonstrated in this case: persistent hiccups and rhabdomyolysis. It reviews the pathophysiology behind these findings, why they should raise red flags for underlying electrolyte disturbances, and their particular relevance in neuroinflammatory conditions. Includes practical takeaways for the ED physician evaluating patients with non-specific neurological symptoms, and a brief overview of conservative SIADH management with fluid restriction versus pharmacologic intervention.
